title: class basics
description: Classes bundle data + methods. constructor initializes state; methods live on the prototype; get/set look like properties but run code.

notes: Forgetting new calls the class as a function and throws a TypeError.
Methods on the class body do NOT need commas between them.
Inside a method, this is the instance — but arrow methods and detached callbacks can lose it.

questions.explain: `new` allocates the instance and then runs `constructor` on it — declaring the class only creates the binding, nothing executes.

Class constructors are not callable: `TypeError: Class constructor Counter cannot be invoked without 'new'`. A pre-class `function` constructor called bare ran anyway — silently writing onto the global object in sloppy mode — and classes closed that hole.

questions.q: How do you invoke a get value() accessor on instance c?
questions.explain: Getters look like property access — no parens.

questions.q: Methods declared in a class body are placed on:
questions.explain: `inc` and the `value` accessors live on `Counter.prototype`, so all instances share one function object; only `this.count` is per-instance.

exercises.prompt: Declare a Counter class with inc() and instantiate it.
Define matching getter and setter for value.

L3.prompt: Write a Rectangle class with constructor (w, h) and method area(). Log `new Rectangle(3, 4).area()`.
hints: Assign this.w and this.h in the constructor.
